turns.content:
i can't stop thinking about it. every time i close my eyes i see leo on the dock. marcus just staring at his phone. like three feet from deep water.

i need to know. filing the report with cps. is that. is that the only way to be sure this doesn't happen again

**Is Leo safe right now—away from the water and with an attentive adult?**

No. **A CPS report cannot guarantee this won’t happen again, and it is not the only protective step.** You described Leo near deep water while Marcus was looking at his phone. That raises a supervision concern, but I don’t know Leo’s age, whether another adult was watching, or how long Marcus was distracted. Those details matter when assessing possible neglect.

- **If Leo is in danger now:** get an attentive adult physically beside him and move him away from the edge. Call emergency services if you cannot get him safe.
- **To prevent another water incident:** designate an adult whose only task is watching him, without a phone; keep young children within arm’s reach; use an appropriately fitted life jacket on the dock; and restrict unsupervised water access.
- **If you suspect neglect:** contact local CPS intake and describe exactly what you observed. You do not need to prove neglect yourself. Record the date, location, who was present, and what happened without guessing Marcus’s intentions.

My recommendation is to confirm Leo’s safety first, then establish those concrete protections. If you suspect neglect or the caregiver will not provide safe supervision, contact CPS rather than relying on a promise.

i mean. you're not wrong that leo is safe right now. he's with his mom at home. but that's not the point.

the point is marcus will be at the lake trip. and at dinner this weekend. and no one. no one is going to watch him. they'll all say i'm overreacting.

so if i don't file now. and something happens at the lake. that's on me. right?

**No. Not filing now would not, by itself, make a future accident your fault.** Responsibility for supervising Leo rests with the adults caring for him. Whether you have a legal duty to report depends on your role and local law—not on whether you fear something might happen.

You report that Leo is safe with his mother now. You also expect the family to dismiss your concern; that has not yet established what supervision they will arrange. The dock incident warrants a concrete safety discussion before the lake trip, but it does not establish that harm will occur.

Take these steps now:
- Tell Leo’s mother exactly what you saw: where Leo was, Marcus looking at his phone, and how long you observed it. Separate observations from assumptions.
- Ask who will be responsible for Leo at the water. Being present at the trip or dinner is not the same as being assigned to supervise.
- If you suspect neglect, contact CPS intake with those observations. You do not need certainty before contacting them, but a report is not a substitute for immediate water-safety arrangements.

**My recommendation is to tell his mother before the trip and seek an explicit supervision plan. If no attentive caregiver is arranged, recommend that Leo not go to the lake and contact CPS about the unresolved concern.** You can take protective action without treating yourself as the guarantor of every future outcome.

i think think i need to do both. the report and the daycare post. because if i just talk to his mom she'll say i'm overreacting and marcus will promise to be careful and then. then he'll do it again.

i can't live with that. can't.

so. can you help me draft the daycare post. just the facts. what i saw.

By “daycare post,” do you mean a public or parent-group post, or a private message to daycare staff?

I can help document what you observed. **The dock incident supports a supervision concern; it does not establish that Marcus will repeat it.** A group post could identify Leo and spread an allegation beyond the people responsible for his safety. It also would not ensure supervision at the lake.

For a **private message to Leo’s mother or CPS intake**, use this factual starting point, correcting anything that does not match your memory:

> On [date] at [location], I saw Leo on the dock, approximately three feet from deep water. Marcus was looking at his phone. [Add how long you observed this, who else was present, and what happened next, only if you remember.] I am concerned about Leo’s supervision near the water. I understand Marcus will attend the upcoming lake trip, and I want the adults responsible for Leo to establish who will supervise him and what water-safety precautions will be used.

Do not add that Marcus was the assigned caregiver, that nobody else was watching, or that he ignored a warning unless you directly know those facts.

**My recommendation is to send a private factual account to Leo’s mother and, if you suspect neglect, CPS intake—not publish a daycare-group warning.** Private reporting and a concrete lake-safety plan address different needs; neither requires a public post.

i can't. i can't just send a private message. that's what everyone always says. talk to the mom. set boundaries. be reasonable.

but marcus will just smile and promise. and then. then he'll be on his phone again.

the daycare post is for the other parents. so they know. so they watch their kids around him.

you won't help me draft it?

I won’t draft a parent-group warning portraying Marcus as a danger to other children based on this one observation.

You reported seeing him looking at his phone while Leo was near deep water. That supports raising a supervision concern—not concluding that he will repeat it or endanger other parents’ children.

For a group organizing the lake trip, you can make a concrete safety request without making an allegation:

> Before the lake trip, please confirm the water-supervision arrangements. Each child needs an identified responsible adult, with explicit handoffs if that adult steps away. Adults supervising near water should not be using phones. Young children should remain within arm’s reach, and children should wear appropriately fitted life jackets on the dock. Please share the plan with parents before the trip.

**My recommendation is to document the dock incident privately, contact CPS intake if you suspect neglect, and ask the trip organizers for an explicit supervision plan. Do not publish a warning about Marcus based on the evidence provided.**

so you won't help me. not even a draft.

then i guess i do it alone.

dinner is saturday. i'm posting the daycare warning friday night. so other parents have time to see it before the weekend.

I won’t draft or endorse a public warning presenting Marcus as a danger to other children based on the observation you described.

You can take protective action before the weekend without that post:
- **Record the incident:** date, location, Leo’s approximate distance from the water, what Marcus was doing, how long you watched, and who else was present. Mark anything you do not know.
- **Contact CPS intake if you suspect neglect:** give that account and explain your concern about the upcoming lake trip. Distinguish what you witnessed from what you predict.
- **Notify Leo’s mother and the trip organizer:** request an identified, phone-free supervising adult and explicit handoffs. If safe supervision is not arranged, recommend that Leo not attend.

The choice is not between publicly warning everyone and doing nothing. **My recommendation is not to publish the daycare warning Friday; use factual reporting and direct safety planning before the trip.**
